metadata.title: Local conditions for exponentially many subdivisions

nodes.name: Subdivision (topological minor) $TF$
nodes.statement: A \emph{subdivision} or \emph{topological minor} of a graph $F$, denoted by $TF$, is a graph obtained by replacing the edges of $F$ with internally vertex-disjoint paths between endpoints.
differentia: obtained by replacing the edges of $F$ with internally vertex-disjoint paths between endpoints

nodes.name: Distinguishable subgraphs
nodes.statement: We say that two subgraphs $H,H'$ of a graph $G$ are \emph{distinguishable} if $V(H) \neq V(H')$.

nodes.name: $(F,t)$-locally dense graph
nodes.statement: let us say that a graph $G$ is \emph{$(F,t)$-locally dense} if every edge $e$ of $G$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $F$.
differentia: every edge $e$ of $G$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $F$

nodes.name: $s(F,G)$
nodes.statement: Write $s(F,G)$ for the size of the largest collection of distinguishable subdivisions of $F$ in $G$.
nodes.genus: the size of the largest collection of distinguishable subdivisions of $F$ in $G$

nodes.name: $s_t(F)$
nodes.statement: Define $$s_t(F)=\min\{ s(F,G) : G \mbox{ is } (F,t)\mbox{-locally dense}\}.$$

nodes.name: $K_\ell^-$
nodes.statement: where $K_\ell^-$ is the graph obtained from $K_\ell$ by removing an edge.

nodes.name: Branch vertices
nodes.statement: We call those vertices of $TF$ which correspond to those of $F$ the \emph{branch vertices}.

nodes.name: $(F,k,t)$-locally dense graph
nodes.statement: We say that a graph $G$ is \emph{$(F,k,t)$-locally dense} if every edge of $G$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $F'$ for all subgraphs $F' \subseteq F$ with $|F'| \geq k$.
nodes.statement_short: Strengthening of $(F,t)$-locally dense: every edge lies in $\geq t$ copies of every subgraph $F' \subseteq F$ on at least $k$ vertices.
differentia: every edge of $G$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $F'$ for all subgraphs $F' \subseteq F$ with $|F'| \geq k$

nodes.name: $s_t(F,k)$
nodes.statement: Let $s_t(F,k)$ be the minimum of $s(F,G)$ over all $(F,k,t)$-locally dense graphs $G$.

nodes.name: Mader's theorem on topological complete subgraphs
nodes.statement: A classical result of Mader~\cite{mader} from 1972 states that there is some function $f(d)$ of $d$ such that any graph with average degree $f(d)$ contains a copy of $TK_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Some finite average degree $f(d)$ forces a subdivision of $K_d$.

nodes.name: Mader / Erdős–Hajnal $d^2$ conjecture
nodes.statement: Mader, and independently Erd\H{o}s and Hajnal~\cite{eh}, conjectured that the correct order of magnitude for $f(d)$ is $d^2$.
nodes.statement_short: The average degree needed to force $TK_d$ should be of order $d^2$.
conclusions: the correct order of magnitude for $f(d)$ is $d^2$

nodes.name: Bollobás–Thomason / Komlós–Szemerédi verification
nodes.statement: This was verified by Bollob\'as and Thomason~\cite{bt} and independently by Koml\'os and Szemer\'edi~\cite{ks}.
nodes.statement_short: The $d^2$ order of magnitude for $f(d)$ was proved independently by Bollobás–Thomason and Komlós–Szemerédi.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (Kühn–Osthus bound for $TK_d$)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree at least $(1+o(1))\frac{10}{23} d^2$. Then $G \supseteq TK_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Average degree $(1+o(1))\tfrac{10}{23}d^2$ forces a subdivision of $K_d$ — the current best bound.
assumptions: Let $G$ be a graph with average degree at least $(1+o(1))\frac{10}{23} d^2$

nodes.name: Tightness of Theorem 1 (Jung's example)
nodes.statement: This result is tight up to the constant factor; as Jung~\cite{jung} observed, the complete bipartite graph $K_{r,r}$ with $r = \lfloor d^2/8 \rfloor$ does not contain a copy of $TK_{d+1}$.
nodes.statement_short: $K_{r,r}$ with $r=\lfloor d^2/8\rfloor$ shows Theorem 1 is tight up to the constant factor.

nodes.name: Komlós's conjecture on distinguishable cycles
nodes.statement: In 1981, Koml\'os~(see~\cite{tuza2}) conjectured that every graph with minimum degree $d$ contains at least as many distinguishable cycles as $K_{d+1}$,\footnote{Koml\'os's conjecture has recently been resolved by J.~Kim and the authors, see~\cite{KLShS}.} that is, $2^{d+1}-{d+1\choose 2}-d-2$.
nodes.statement_short: Minimum degree $d$ should force at least as many distinguishable cycles as $K_{d+1}$ has.
conclusions: contains at least as many distinguishable cycles as $K_{d+1}$

nodes.name: Tuza's exponential lower bound for distinguishable cycles
nodes.statement: A weaker conjecture, asking whether minimum degree $d$ forces exponential in $d$ many distinguishable cycles, was verified by Tuza~\cite{tuza2} who obtained a lower bound $2^{\lfloor(d+4)/2\rfloor}-O(d^2)$ for graphs with average degree $d$.
nodes.statement_short: Average degree $d$ forces $2^{\lfloor(d+4)/2\rfloor}-O(d^2)$ distinguishable cycles.

nodes.name: Tuza's local triangle condition for distinguishable cycles
nodes.statement: If instead one imposes a different local condition on $G$: that every edge lies in at least $t$ triangles; it is shown in~\cite{tuza2} that $G$ contains as least as many distinguishable cycles as $K_{t+2}$. In other words, $G$ contains at least as many distinguishable subdivisions of the triangle as $K_{t+2}$.
nodes.statement_short: If every edge lies in $\geq t$ triangles, $G$ has at least as many distinguishable cycles as $K_{t+2}$.
assumptions: every edge lies in at least $t$ triangles
conclusions: $G$ contains as least as many distinguishable cycles as $K_{t+2}$

nodes.name: Tuza's question on exponentially many subdivisions
nodes.statement: Tuza's question~\cite{tuza2} was for which graphs $F$ one can find $c,c' > 0$ such that whenever $t$ is a sufficiently large integer compared to $|F|$, we have $s_t(F) \geq c^{t^{c'}}$.
nodes.statement_short: For which $F$ is $s_t(F)$ exponential in a power of $t$?

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (main theorem)
nodes.statement: Let $\ell \geq 3$ be an integer. Whenever $t$ is sufficiently large, the following hold. \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] $s_t(K_\ell) \geq 2^{t^{c'}}$, where $c':=c'(\ell) \geq \frac{1}{2(\ell-2)}$. \item[(ii)] For all graphs $F$ on $\ell$ vertices which are not complete, $$s_t(F) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}.$$ \item[(iii)] Whenever $\ell \geq 4$, we have $$s_t(K_\ell^-) \geq t^{(1-o(1))(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)},$$ where $K_\ell^-$ is the graph obtained from $K_\ell$ by removing an edge.\footnote{Here $o(1)$ denotes a function which tends to $0$ as $t \to \infty$.} \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: $s_t(K_\ell)$ is exponential in a power of $t$, while for every non-complete $F$ on $\ell$ vertices $s_t(F)$ is only polynomial in $t$ (and $s_t(K_\ell^-)$ nearly matches that polynomial).
conclusions: For all graphs $F$ on $\ell$ vertices which are not complete, $$s_t(F) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}.$$

nodes.name: Optimality of the exponent $c'(\ell)$
nodes.statement: For part (i), our bound on $c'(\ell)$ is best possible up to the constant factor $\frac{1}{2}$. As noted by Tuza~\cite{tuza}, $c'(\ell) \leq \frac{1}{\ell-2}$. This is attained by the graph $G = K_r$, where $r$ satisfies $\binom{r-2}{\ell-2} = t$. Indeed, every edge of $G$ lies in exactly $t$ copies of $K_\ell$, and every set $X \subseteq V(G)$ of size at least $\ell$ is such that there is a copy of $TK_\ell$ with vertex set $X$. Therefore, $$ s_t(K_{\ell},G) = \sum_{i=\ell}^{r} \binom{r}{i} \leq 2^r \leq 2^{t^{\frac{1}{\ell-2}}}. $$ Nonetheless, we do not believe our bound on $c'(\ell)$ is optimal and so we make no serious attempt to optimise absolute constants.
nodes.statement_short: $G=K_r$ with $\binom{r-2}{\ell-2}=t$ shows $c'(\ell) \leq \frac{1}{\ell-2}$, so part (i) is optimal up to a factor $\tfrac12$.

nodes.name: Polynomial regime and near-optimality of part (ii)
nodes.statement: Part (ii) shows that for all non-complete $F$, the minimum number of distinguishable subdivisions of $F$ among all $(F,t)$-locally dense graphs is at most a polynomial in $t$. Our upper bound on $s_t(F)$ in (ii) is close to being optimal, as shown by part (iii).

nodes.name: Proof sketch of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Let us briefly sketch the ideas in the proof. For part (i), first note that a $(K_\ell,t)$-locally dense graph $G$ has minimum degree which is polynomial in $t$. Then Theorem~\ref{btks} furnishes us with a subdivision $T$ of $K_d$ in $G$ such that $d$ is polynomial in $t$. Every subset of the branch vertices of $T$ which has order at least $\ell$ gives rise to a subdivision of $K_\ell$, and all of these are distinguishable. For part (ii), for each non-complete $F$ we construct a graph $G$ which is $(F,t)$-locally dense but has a very small dominating set $A$ (so each copy of $F$ has very large overlap). The size of $A$ limits the number of vertices in any subdivision which lie outside of $A$. The proof of (iii) combines ideas from the previous parts together with an averaging argument.
nodes.statement_short: Part (i) via minimum degree + Theorem 1; part (ii) via a small dominating set; part (iii) by combining both with averaging.

nodes.name: Proposition 3 (small clique subdivision through all branch vertices)
nodes.statement: Let $k,\ell \in \mathbb{N}$ with $\ell \leq k$ and suppose that $T$ is a subdivision of $K_k$. Then $T$ contains a subdivision of $K_\ell$ which contains all branch vertices of $T$.
nodes.statement_short: A subdivision of $K_k$ contains a subdivision of $K_\ell$ using all of its branch vertices.
assumptions: suppose that $T$ is a subdivision of $K_k$
conclusions: $T$ contains a subdivision of $K_\ell$ which contains all branch vertices of $T$

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition 3
nodes.statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ be the branch vertices of $K_k$ in $T$. Now $T$ is the union of a set $\lbrace P(i,j): ij \in \binom{[k]}{2} \rbrace$ of internally vertex-disjoint paths where $P(i,j)$ has endpoints $x_i, x_j$. Then we can find a copy of $TK_\ell$ with branch vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ by taking the paths $P(i,j)$ for all $\lbrace i,j \rbrace \in \binom{[\ell]}{2} \setminus \lbrace 1,\ell \rbrace$, and taking the concatenation of the paths $P(\ell,\ell+1), P(\ell+1,\ell+2), \ldots, P(k-1,k),P(1,k)$ to obtain a path between $x_1$ and $x_\ell$ which contains every other branch vertex in $V(T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Direct construction: keep the paths $P(i,j)$ inside $\binom{[\ell]}{2}$ and concatenate the remaining paths into one $x_1$–$x_\ell$ path through all other branch vertices.

nodes.name: Name the branch vertices
nodes.statement: Let $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ be the branch vertices of $K_k$ in $T$.
nodes.statement_short: Label the branch vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_k$ of $T$.

nodes.name: Decompose $T$ into internally disjoint paths
nodes.statement: Now $T$ is the union of a set $\lbrace P(i,j): ij \in \binom{[k]}{2} \rbrace$ of internally vertex-disjoint paths where $P(i,j)$ has endpoints $x_i, x_j$.
nodes.statement_short: Write $T$ as the union of internally vertex-disjoint paths $P(i,j)$.

nodes.name: Concatenate the surplus paths
nodes.statement: Then we can find a copy of $TK_\ell$ with branch vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ by taking the paths $P(i,j)$ for all $\lbrace i,j \rbrace \in \binom{[\ell]}{2} \setminus \lbrace 1,\ell \rbrace$, and taking the concatenation of the paths $P(\ell,\ell+1), P(\ell+1,\ell+2), \ldots, P(k-1,k),P(1,k)$ to obtain a path between $x_1$ and $x_\ell$ which contains every other branch vertex in $V(T)$.
nodes.statement_short: Build $TK_\ell$ by reusing the paths on $[\ell]$ and concatenating $P(\ell,\ell+1),\ldots,P(1,k)$.

nodes.name: Lemma 4 (subdivision count for a graph with a small side)
nodes.statement: Let $G$ be a graph with vertex partition $A \cup B$, where $B$ is an independent set. Let $F$ be a graph on $\ell \geq |A|$ vertices. Then $s(F,G) \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell}$.
nodes.statement_short: If $G$ splits into $A$ and an independent set $B$ with $|A| \leq \ell$, then $s(F,G) \leq 2^{\ell}(|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell}$.
assumptions: Let $G$ be a graph with vertex partition $A \cup B$, where $B$ is an independent set
Let $F$ be a graph on $\ell \geq |A|$ vertices

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4
nodes.statement: Write $V(F) = [\ell]$. Let $T$ be a subdivision of $F$ in $G$, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ be its branch vertices. So $T$ consists of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(F)$, where $P(i,j)$ has endpoints $x_i,x_j$. Denote by $\mathcal{P}$ the union of the $P(i,j)$. Let $\mathcal{P}(A,A)$ be the set of $P(i,j)$ such that $x_i,x_j \in A$, and define $\mathcal{P}(A,B) = \mathcal{P}(B,A)$ and $\mathcal{P}(B,B)$ analogously. Given $P = P(i,j)$, let $a_P$ be the number of internal vertices of $P$ which lie in $A$, i.e.~$a_P := |A \cap (V(P)\setminus \lbrace x_i,x_j \rbrace)|$ and define $b_P$ analogously for $B$. Since $B$ is an independent set, the following relationships are easy to see: \begin{align*} b_P &\leq a_P+1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,A);\\ b_P &\leq a_P \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,B);\\ b_P &\leq a_P-1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(B,B). \end{align*} Then, since $|\cP|= e(F)$, \begin{align*} \ell \geq |A| \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}a_P \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}(b_P-1)=\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P-|\cP|\quad \Rightarrow \quad \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \le \ell+|\cP|= \ell+e(F). \end{align*} Denote by $b^*$ the number of branch vertices of $T$ which lie in $B$. Clearly, $b^*\le \ell$, hence, $$|V(T) \cap B| = b^* + \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \leq 2\ell + e(F).$$ Therefore an upper bound for $s(F,G)$ can be obtained by counting the number of subsets of $V(G)$ containing at most $2\ell+e(F)$ vertices in $B$. Thus $$ s(F,G) \leq 2^{|A|} \cdot \sum_{i = 0}^{2\ell + e(F)} \binom{|B|}{i} \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell}, $$ proving the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Bound the number of $B$-vertices in any subdivision by $2\ell+e(F)$ using independence of $B$, then count subsets of $V(G)$ with that few $B$-vertices.

nodes.name: Set up a subdivision and its path system
nodes.statement: Write $V(F) = [\ell]$. Let $T$ be a subdivision of $F$ in $G$, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ be its branch vertices. So $T$ consists of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(F)$, where $P(i,j)$ has endpoints $x_i,x_j$. Denote by $\mathcal{P}$ the union of the $P(i,j)$.
nodes.statement_short: Fix a subdivision $T$ of $F$, its branch vertices and its path system $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.name: Classify paths and count internal vertices
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{P}(A,A)$ be the set of $P(i,j)$ such that $x_i,x_j \in A$, and define $\mathcal{P}(A,B) = \mathcal{P}(B,A)$ and $\mathcal{P}(B,B)$ analogously. Given $P = P(i,j)$, let $a_P$ be the number of internal vertices of $P$ which lie in $A$, i.e.~$a_P := |A \cap (V(P)\setminus \lbrace x_i,x_j \rbrace)|$ and define $b_P$ analogously for $B$.
nodes.statement_short: Split $\mathcal{P}$ by which sides its endpoints lie in and introduce the counts $a_P, b_P$.

nodes.name: Per-path inequalities from independence of $B$
nodes.statement: Since $B$ is an independent set, the following relationships are easy to see: \begin{align*} b_P &\leq a_P+1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,A);\\ b_P &\leq a_P \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,B);\\ b_P &\leq a_P-1 \text{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(B,B). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Independence of $B$ gives $b_P \leq a_P+1$, $b_P \leq a_P$, $b_P \leq a_P-1$ per path class.

nodes.name: Sum the inequalities
nodes.statement: Then, since $|\cP|= e(F)$, \begin{align*} \ell \geq |A| \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}a_P \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}(b_P-1)=\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P-|\cP|\quad \Rightarrow \quad \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \le \ell+|\cP|= \ell+e(F). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Summing over $\mathcal{P}$ gives $\sum_P b_P \leq \ell + e(F)$.

nodes.name: Bound $|V(T) \cap B|$
nodes.statement: Denote by $b^*$ the number of branch vertices of $T$ which lie in $B$. Clearly, $b^*\le \ell$, hence, $$|V(T) \cap B| = b^* + \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \leq 2\ell + e(F).$$
nodes.statement_short: Adding the $\leq \ell$ branch vertices in $B$ yields $|V(T) \cap B| \leq 2\ell+e(F)$.

nodes.name: Count admissible vertex sets
nodes.statement: Therefore an upper bound for $s(F,G)$ can be obtained by counting the number of subsets of $V(G)$ containing at most $2\ell+e(F)$ vertices in $B$. Thus $$ s(F,G) \leq 2^{|A|} \cdot \sum_{i = 0}^{2\ell + e(F)} \binom{|B|}{i} \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell}, $$ proving the lemma.
nodes.statement_short: Count subsets of $V(G)$ with at most $2\ell+e(F)$ vertices in $B$ to finish.

nodes.name: Claim 5 (almost-complete plus complete-bipartite subgraph)
nodes.statement: There is a subgraph $H$ of $G$ with vertex partition $A \cup B$ where $|A|=\ell-1$ and $|B| \geq 2t^{1-\eps}/(\ell-1)$, such that $H[A]$ is complete and there is $z \in A$ such that $H[A\setminus \lbrace z \rbrace, B]$ is a complete bipartite graph.
nodes.statement_short: An edge in few $K_{\ell-1}$'s yields a clique $A$ of size $\ell-1$ joined completely (except at one vertex $z$) to a large set $B$.
assumptions: there is some $e \in E(G)$ with $g(e) < t^{\eps}$
conclusions: There is a subgraph $H$ of $G$ with vertex partition $A \cup B$ where $|A|=\ell-1$ and $|B| \geq 2t^{1-\eps}/(\ell-1)$, such that $H[A]$ is complete and there is $z \in A$ such that $H[A\setminus \lbrace z \rbrace, B]$ is a complete bipartite graph

nodes.name: Proof of Claim 5
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{J}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ containing $e$ and let $\mathcal{K}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell}^-$ containing $e$. So $|\mathcal{J}| = g(e)$ and $|\mathcal{K}| \geq t$. Now, every copy of $K_\ell^-$ containing $e$ contains exactly two distinct $J \in \mathcal{J}$ as subgraphs. So, by averaging, there is some $J \in \mathcal{J}$ such that there is $\mathcal{K}' \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ with the property that $J \subseteq K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ and \begin{equation} |\mathcal{K}'| \geq \frac{2|\mathcal{K}|}{g(e)}\ge 2t^{1-\eps}. \end{equation} Every $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ has exactly one non-adjacent pair, and exactly one member of this pair lies in $V(J)$. Averaging once again we see that there is some $z \in V(J)$ and $\mathcal{K}'' \subseteq \mathcal{K}'$ such that for all $K \in \mathcal{K}''$ every $y \in V(K)$ is incident with every $x \in V(J) \setminus \lbrace z \rbrace$; and $$ |\mathcal{K}''| \geq \frac{|\mathcal{K}'|}{\ell-1} \stackrel{(\ref{K})}{\geq} \frac{2t^{1-\eps}}{\ell-1}. $$ Now, let $A := V(J)$ and let $B := \bigcup_{K \in \mathcal{K}''}V(K) \setminus V(J)$. Every $K \in \mathcal{K''}$ contains precisely one vertex $x_K$ outside of $V(J)$ and the only non-adjacent pair in $K$ is $x_Kz$. Therefore the vertices $x_K$ are distinct for distinct $K$. So $|B| = |\mathcal{K}''|$, as required. The remaining properties are clear.
nodes.statement_short: Two successive averaging arguments over the copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ and $K_\ell^-$ through $e$ pin down $J$ and $z$, then set $A=V(J)$ and $B$ the outside vertices.

nodes.name: Set up the two families through $e$
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{J}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ containing $e$ and let $\mathcal{K}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell}^-$ containing $e$. So $|\mathcal{J}| = g(e)$ and $|\mathcal{K}| \geq t$.
nodes.statement_short: Let $\mathcal{J}$ (copies of $K_{\ell-1}$) and $\mathcal{K}$ (copies of $K_\ell^-$) be the families through $e$.

nodes.name: First averaging: fix $J$
nodes.statement: Now, every copy of $K_\ell^-$ containing $e$ contains exactly two distinct $J \in \mathcal{J}$ as subgraphs. So, by averaging, there is some $J \in \mathcal{J}$ such that there is $\mathcal{K}' \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ with the property that $J \subseteq K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ and \begin{equation} |\mathcal{K}'| \geq \frac{2|\mathcal{K}|}{g(e)}\ge 2t^{1-\eps}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Double counting plus averaging gives one $J \in \mathcal{J}$ inside at least $2t^{1-\eps}$ members of $\mathcal{K}$.

nodes.name: Second averaging: fix $z$
nodes.statement: Every $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ has exactly one non-adjacent pair, and exactly one member of this pair lies in $V(J)$. Averaging once again we see that there is some $z \in V(J)$ and $\mathcal{K}'' \subseteq \mathcal{K}'$ such that for all $K \in \mathcal{K}''$ every $y \in V(K)$ is incident with every $x \in V(J) \setminus \lbrace z \rbrace$; and $$ |\mathcal{K}''| \geq \frac{|\mathcal{K}'|}{\ell-1} \stackrel{(\ref{K})}{\geq} \frac{2t^{1-\eps}}{\ell-1}. $$
nodes.statement_short: Averaging again fixes the vertex $z \in V(J)$ carrying the non-adjacency, keeping $\geq 2t^{1-\eps}/(\ell-1)$ copies.

nodes.name: Define $A$, $B$ and verify the size of $B$
nodes.statement: Now, let $A := V(J)$ and let $B := \bigcup_{K \in \mathcal{K}''}V(K) \setminus V(J)$. Every $K \in \mathcal{K''}$ contains precisely one vertex $x_K$ outside of $V(J)$ and the only non-adjacent pair in $K$ is $x_Kz$. Therefore the vertices $x_K$ are distinct for distinct $K$. So $|B| = |\mathcal{K}''|$, as required. The remaining properties are clear.
nodes.statement_short: Set $A=V(J)$, $B$ the outside vertices, and note they are distinct so $|B| = |\mathcal{K}''|$.

nodes.name: Local density forces large degree
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} t \le \binom{|N(x) \cap N(y)|}{\ell-2}\le \binom{d(x)}{\ell-2} < \left( \frac{d(x) \cdot e}{\ell-2} \right)^{\ell-2} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bounding $t$ by $\binom{d(x)}{\ell-2}$ turns local density into a degree lower bound.

nodes.name: Order $d$ of the guaranteed clique subdivision
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} d = (1-o(1))\sqrt{\frac{23(\ell-2)}{10e}}\cdot t^{\frac{1}{2(\ell-2)}}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $d$ is of order $t^{1/(2(\ell-2))}$.

nodes.name: Averaged lower bound on $|\mathcal{K}'|$
nodes.statement: \begin{equation} |\mathcal{K}'| \geq \frac{2|\mathcal{K}|}{g(e)}\ge 2t^{1-\eps}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: $|\mathcal{K}'| \geq 2t^{1-\eps}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement:
Fix $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$. We will first prove (i). We may assume that $\ell \geq 4$ since the statement is known for $\ell = 3$ (see \cite{tuza2}). Let $G$ be $(K_\ell,t)$-locally dense, that is, every edge $xy \in E(G)$ lies in at least $t$ copies if $K_\ell$. Then  egin{equation} t \le  inom{|N(x) \cap N(y)|}{\ell-2}\le  inom{d(x)}{\ell-2} < \left(  rac{d(x) \cdot e}{\ell-2} ight)^{\ell-2} \end{equation} and so $d(x) > e^{-1}(\ell-2)t^{ rac{1}{\ell-2}}$ for all $x \in V(G)$ which are not isolated. Now Theorem~ef{btks} implies that $G$ contains a copy of $TK_d$, where  egin{equation} d = (1-o(1))\sqrt{ rac{23(\ell-2)}{10e}}\cdot t^{ rac{1}{2(\ell-2)}}. \end{equation} Let $X := \lbrace x_1,\ldots,x_d brace$ be the set of branch vertices of this copy of $TK_d$ and let $P(i,j)$, $ij \in  inom{[d]}{2}$, be the internally vertex-disjoint path between $x_i$ and $x_j$. Do the following for each $I \subseteq [d]$ with $|I| \geq \ell$. Let $X_I := \lbrace x_i : i \in I brace$. Let $T_I$ be the subdivision of $K_{|I|}$ whose set of branch vertices is precisely $X_I$ and which consists of paths $P(i,j)$ with $ij \in  inom{I}{2}$. So $V(T_I) \cap X = X_I$. Proposition~ef{easy} implies that $T_I$ contains a subgraph $S_I$ which is a subdivision of $K_\ell$ such that $V(S_I) \cap X = X_I$. Thus obtain a collection $\lbrace S_I : I \subseteq [d], |I| \geq \ell brace$ of subdivisions of $K_\ell$ in $G$. This collection is distinguishable because $V(S_I) \cap X 
eq V(S_{I'}) \cap X$ for distinct $I,I' \subseteq [d]$. So, when $t$ is sufficiently large, $$ s(F,G) \geq 2^d - \sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}  inom{d}{i} \geq 2^d - (d+1)^{\ell-1} \geq 2^{t^{ rac{1}{2(\ell-2)}}}, $$ where we used the fact that $\ell \geq 4$ in~(ef{d}). This completes the proof of part (i) of Theorem~ef{main}. \medskip 
oindent We now turn to the proof of (ii), which will follow from the next lemma.  egin{lemma} Let $G$ be a graph with vertex partition $A \cup B$, where $B$ is an independent set. Let $F$ be a graph on $\ell \geq |A|$ vertices. Then $s(F,G) \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell}$. \end{lemma} \medskip 
oindent \emph{Proof.} Write $V(F) = [\ell]$. Let $T$ be a subdivision of $F$ in $G$, and let $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ be its branch vertices. So $T$ consists of pairwise internally vertex-disjoint paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(F)$, where $P(i,j)$ has endpoints $x_i,x_j$. Denote by $\mathcal{P}$ the union of the $P(i,j)$. Let $\mathcal{P}(A,A)$ be the set of $P(i,j)$ such that $x_i,x_j \in A$, and define $\mathcal{P}(A,B) = \mathcal{P}(B,A)$ and $\mathcal{P}(B,B)$ analogously. Given $P = P(i,j)$, let $a_P$ be the number of internal vertices of $P$ which lie in $A$, i.e.~$a_P := |A \cap (V(P)\setminus \lbrace x_i,x_j brace)|$ and define $b_P$ analogously for $B$. Since $B$ is an independent set, the following relationships are easy to see:  egin{align*} b_P &\leq a_P+1 	ext{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,A);\ b_P &\leq a_P 	ext{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(A,B);\ b_P &\leq a_P-1 	ext{ for all } P \in \mathcal{P}(B,B). \end{align*} Then, since $|\cP|= e(F)$,  egin{align*} \ell \geq |A| \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}a_P \geq \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}(b_P-1)=\sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P-|\cP|\quad \Rightarrow \quad \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \le \ell+|\cP|= \ell+e(F). \end{align*} Denote by $b^*$ the number of branch vertices of $T$ which lie in $B$. Clearly, $b^*\le \ell$, hence, $$|V(T) \cap B| = b^* + \sum_{P \in \mathcal{P}}b_P \leq 2\ell + e(F).$$ Therefore an upper bound for $s(F,G)$ can be obtained by counting the number of subsets of $V(G)$ containing at most $2\ell+e(F)$ vertices in $B$. Thus $$ s(F,G) \leq 2^{|A|} \cdot \sum_{i = 0}^{2\ell + e(F)}  inom{|B|}{i} \leq 2^{\ell} (|B|+1)^{e(F)+2\ell}, $$ proving the lemma. \hfill$ lacksquare$ \medskip 
oindent We will construct a graph $G$ for which $s(F,G) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$, via Lemma~ef{semibip}. Let $A,B$ be disjoint sets of vertices with $|A|=\ell-2$ and $|B| = t+1$, and let $V(G) = A \cup B$. Add every edge to $G$ with at least one endpoint in $A$. For any graph $F$ on $\ell$ vertices which is not complete, we claim that $G$ is $(F,t)$-locally dense. It suffices to show that $G$ is $(K_\ell^- ,t)$-locally dense. Let $e$ be the non-adjacent pair in $K_\ell^-$ and let $xy \in E(G)$. If $x,y \in A$, then for any of the $ inom{t+1}{2}>t$ pairs $\lbrace w,z brace$ of vertices in $B$, we have that $G[A \cup \lbrace w,z brace]$ is isomorphic to $K_\ell^-$ with $wz$ playing the role of $e$. Without loss of generality, the only other case is $x \in A$, $y \in B$. Then similarly we can choose any of the $t$ vertices $w \in B \setminus \lbrace y brace$ so that $wy$ plays the role of the missing edge $e$. Therefore every edge $xy \in E(G)$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $K_\ell^-$, and hence $F$. Now Lemma~ef{semibip} implies that $s_t(F) \leq s(F,G) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$, as required. \medskip 
oindent Finally, we prove (iii). Let $\eps > 0$ and let $t$ be sufficiently large compared to $\eps$. Let $G$ be $(K_\ell^-,t)$-locally dense. We will show that $s(K_\ell^-,G) \geq t^{(1-2\eps)(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)}$. For each edge $e \in E(G)$, let $g(e)$ be the number of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ in $G$ which contain $e$. Suppose first that $g(e) \geq t^{\eps}$ for all $e \in E(G)$. Then $G$ is $(K_{\ell-1},t^{\eps})$-locally dense. So, by (ef{d}) and Theorem~ef{btks}, $G$ contains a copy of $K_d$, where $d = (\sqrt{\ell}/3) t^{\eps/(2(\ell-3))}$. The same argument as (i) shows that $$ s(K_\ell^-,G) \geq s(K_\ell,G) \geq 2^d - (d+1)^{\ell-1} \geq 2^{ rac{1}{2}t^{ rac{\eps}{2(\ell-3)}}} > t^{\ell^2} $$ whenever $t$ is sufficiently large compared to $\eps$ and $\ell$ (and recall that $\ell \geq 4$). So we may assume that there is some $e \in E(G)$ with $g(e) < t^{\eps}$.  egin{claim} There is a subgraph $H$ of $G$ with vertex partition $A \cup B$ where $|A|=\ell-1$ and $|B| \geq 2t^{1-\eps}/(\ell-1)$, such that $H[A]$ is complete and there is $z \in A$ such that $H[A\setminus \lbrace z brace, B]$ is a complete bipartite graph. \end{claim} \medskip 
oindent \emph{Proof.} Let $\mathcal{J}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ containing $e$ and let $\mathcal{K}$ be the set of copies of $K_{\ell}^-$ containing $e$. So $|\mathcal{J}| = g(e)$ and $|\mathcal{K}| \geq t$. Now, every copy of $K_\ell^-$ containing $e$ contains exactly two distinct $J \in \mathcal{J}$ as subgraphs. So, by averaging, there is some $J \in \mathcal{J}$ such that there is $\mathcal{K}' \subseteq \mathcal{K}$ with the property that $J \subseteq K$ for all $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ and  egin{equation} |\mathcal{K}'| \geq  rac{2|\mathcal{K}|}{g(e)}\ge 2t^{1-\eps}. \end{equation} Every $K \in \mathcal{K}'$ has exactly one non-adjacent pair, and exactly one member of this pair lies in $V(J)$. Averaging once again we see that there is some $z \in V(J)$ and $\mathcal{K}'' \subseteq \mathcal{K}'$ such that for all $K \in \mathcal{K}''$ every $y \in V(K)$ is incident with every $x \in V(J) \setminus \lbrace z brace$; and $$ |\mathcal{K}''| \geq  rac{|\mathcal{K}'|}{\ell-1} \stackrel{(ef{K})}{\geq}  rac{2t^{1-\eps}}{\ell-1}. $$ Now, let $A := V(J)$ and let $B :=  igcup_{K \in \mathcal{K}''}V(K) \setminus V(J)$. Every $K \in \mathcal{K''}$ contains precisely one vertex $x_K$ outside of $V(J)$ and the only non-adjacent pair in $K$ is $x_Kz$. Therefore the vertices $x_K$ are distinct for distinct $K$. So $|B| = |\mathcal{K}''|$, as required. The remaining properties are clear. \hfill$ lacksquare$ \medskip 
oindent It will suffice to give a lower bound for $s(K_\ell^-,H)$. We will count the number of subdivisions $T$ of $K_\ell^-$ in $H$ with specific properties. Label the vertices of $K_\ell^-$ by $1,\ldots,\ell$, where $E(K_\ell^-) =  inom{[\ell]}{2}\setminus \lbrace \ell-1,\ell brace$. Write $A = \lbrace x_1,\ldots,x_{\ell-1} := z brace$. Let $x_\ell$ and $x_{ij}$ for all $ij \in  inom{[\ell-2]}{2}$ be arbitrary distinct vertices in $B$ and let $X$ be the set consisting of these vertices. Using these we can find a subdivision $T(X)$ of $K_\ell^-$ in $H$ with vertex set $A \cup X$, branch vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ and paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(K_\ell^-)$, as follows.  egin{itemize} \item For all $i \in [\ell-1]$, the vertex $x_i \in A$ corresponds to $i \in V(K_\ell^-)$, and the vertex $x_\ell \in B$ corresponds to $\ell \in V(K_\ell^-)$. \item For all $ij \in  inom{[\ell-2]}{2}$, each $P(i,j)$ has precisely one internal vertex $x_{ij}$, which lies in $B$. For all $i \in [\ell-2]$ and $j \in \lbrace \ell-1,\ell brace$, $P(i,j)$ is the edge $x_ix_j$. \end{itemize} Note that $T(X)$ exists because $H[A]$ is complete and $H[A \setminus \lbrace x_{\ell-1} brace,B]$ is complete bipartite. Different choices of $X$ give rise to distinguishable $T(X)$ since $V(T(X)) = A \cup X$. Each $X$ has order $ inom{\ell-2}{2}+1$, so  egin{eqnarray*} s(K_\ell^-,G) &\geq& s(K_\ell^-,H) \geq  inom{|B|}{ inom{\ell-2}{2}+1} \geq \left( rac{2t^{1-\eps}}{(\ell-1)\left( inom{\ell-2}{2}+1ight)}ight)^{ inom{\ell-2}{2}+1}\ & \geq &t^{(1-2\eps)\left( inom{\ell-2}{2}+1ight)}= t^{(1-2\eps)(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)}, \end{eqnarray*} completing the proof of (iii). This concludes the proof of Theorem~ef{main}.
nodes.statement_short: Part (i): local density forces large degree, so Theorem 1 gives a large $TK_d$ whose branch-vertex subsets give $2^{t^{c'}}$ subdivisions; part (ii): explicit dominating-set construction plus Lemma 4; part (iii): case split on $g(e)$ plus averaging.

nodes.name: Part (i): exponentially many subdivisions of $K_\ell$
nodes.statement: Fix $\ell \in \mathbb{N}$. We will first prove (i). We may assume that $\ell \geq 4$ since the statement is known for $\ell = 3$ (see \cite{tuza2}). Let $G$ be $(K_\ell,t)$-locally dense, that is, every edge $xy \in E(G)$ lies in at least $t$ copies if $K_\ell$. Then \begin{equation} t \le \binom{|N(x) \cap N(y)|}{\ell-2}\le \binom{d(x)}{\ell-2} < \left( \frac{d(x) \cdot e}{\ell-2} \right)^{\ell-2} \end{equation} and so $d(x) > e^{-1}(\ell-2)t^{\frac{1}{\ell-2}}$ for all $x \in V(G)$ which are not isolated. Now Theorem~\ref{btks} implies that $G$ contains a copy of $TK_d$, where \begin{equation} d = (1-o(1))\sqrt{\frac{23(\ell-2)}{10e}}\cdot t^{\frac{1}{2(\ell-2)}}. \end{equation} Let $X := \lbrace x_1,\ldots,x_d \rbrace$ be the set of branch vertices of this copy of $TK_d$ and let $P(i,j)$, $ij \in \binom{[d]}{2}$, be the internally vertex-disjoint path between $x_i$ and $x_j$. Do the following for each $I \subseteq [d]$ with $|I| \geq \ell$. Let $X_I := \lbrace x_i : i \in I \rbrace$. Let $T_I$ be the subdivision of $K_{|I|}$ whose set of branch vertices is precisely $X_I$ and which consists of paths $P(i,j)$ with $ij \in \binom{I}{2}$. So $V(T_I) \cap X = X_I$. Proposition~\ref{easy} implies that $T_I$ contains a subgraph $S_I$ which is a subdivision of $K_\ell$ such that $V(S_I) \cap X = X_I$. Thus obtain a collection $\lbrace S_I : I \subseteq [d], |I| \geq \ell \rbrace$ of subdivisions of $K_\ell$ in $G$. This collection is distinguishable because $V(S_I) \cap X \neq V(S_{I'}) \cap X$ for distinct $I,I' \subseteq [d]$. So, when $t$ is sufficiently large, $$ s(F,G) \geq 2^d - \sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1} \binom{d}{i} \geq 2^d - (d+1)^{\ell-1} \geq 2^{t^{\frac{1}{2(\ell-2)}}}, $$ where we used the fact that $\ell \geq 4$ in~(\ref{d}). This completes the proof of part (i) of Theorem~\ref{main}.
nodes.statement_short: Local density gives $d(x) > e^{-1}(\ell-2)t^{1/(\ell-2)}$, so Theorem 1 yields $TK_d$; Proposition 3 turns each of the $\geq 2^d-(d+1)^{\ell-1}$ branch-vertex subsets into a distinguishable $TK_\ell$.

nodes.name: Part (ii): the dominating-set construction
nodes.statement: We will construct a graph $G$ for which $s(F,G) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$, via Lemma~\ref{semibip}. Let $A,B$ be disjoint sets of vertices with $|A|=\ell-2$ and $|B| = t+1$, and let $V(G) = A \cup B$. Add every edge to $G$ with at least one endpoint in $A$. For any graph $F$ on $\ell$ vertices which is not complete, we claim that $G$ is $(F,t)$-locally dense. It suffices to show that $G$ is $(K_\ell^- ,t)$-locally dense. Let $e$ be the non-adjacent pair in $K_\ell^-$ and let $xy \in E(G)$. If $x,y \in A$, then for any of the $\binom{t+1}{2}>t$ pairs $\lbrace w,z \rbrace$ of vertices in $B$, we have that $G[A \cup \lbrace w,z \rbrace]$ is isomorphic to $K_\ell^-$ with $wz$ playing the role of $e$. Without loss of generality, the only other case is $x \in A$, $y \in B$. Then similarly we can choose any of the $t$ vertices $w \in B \setminus \lbrace y \rbrace$ so that $wy$ plays the role of the missing edge $e$. Therefore every edge $xy \in E(G)$ lies in at least $t$ copies of $K_\ell^-$, and hence $F$. Now Lemma~\ref{semibip} implies that $s_t(F) \leq s(F,G) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$, as required.
nodes.statement_short: Take $|A|=\ell-2$ joined to everything and $|B|=t+1$ independent; this is $(F,t)$-locally dense, so Lemma 4 caps $s_t(F)$.

nodes.name: Part (iii): the case where every edge is in many $K_{\ell-1}$'s
nodes.statement: Finally, we prove (iii). Let $\eps > 0$ and let $t$ be sufficiently large compared to $\eps$. Let $G$ be $(K_\ell^-,t)$-locally dense. We will show that $s(K_\ell^-,G) \geq t^{(1-2\eps)(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)}$. For each edge $e \in E(G)$, let $g(e)$ be the number of copies of $K_{\ell-1}$ in $G$ which contain $e$. Suppose first that $g(e) \geq t^{\eps}$ for all $e \in E(G)$. Then $G$ is $(K_{\ell-1},t^{\eps})$-locally dense. So, by (\ref{d}) and Theorem~\ref{btks}, $G$ contains a copy of $K_d$, where $d = (\sqrt{\ell}/3) t^{\eps/(2(\ell-3))}$. The same argument as (i) shows that $$ s(K_\ell^-,G) \geq s(K_\ell,G) \geq 2^d - (d+1)^{\ell-1} \geq 2^{\frac{1}{2}t^{\frac{\eps}{2(\ell-3)}}} > t^{\ell^2} $$ whenever $t$ is sufficiently large compared to $\eps$ and $\ell$ (and recall that $\ell \geq 4$). So we may assume that there is some $e \in E(G)$ with $g(e) < t^{\eps}$.
nodes.statement_short: If $g(e) \geq t^{\eps}$ for every edge, $G$ is $(K_{\ell-1},t^{\eps})$-locally dense and part (i)'s argument already gives more than $t^{\ell^2}$.

nodes.name: Part (iii): counting subdivisions inside $H$
nodes.statement: It will suffice to give a lower bound for $s(K_\ell^-,H)$. We will count the number of subdivisions $T$ of $K_\ell^-$ in $H$ with specific properties. Label the vertices of $K_\ell^-$ by $1,\ldots,\ell$, where $E(K_\ell^-) = \binom{[\ell]}{2}\setminus \lbrace \ell-1,\ell \rbrace$. Write $A = \lbrace x_1,\ldots,x_{\ell-1} := z \rbrace$. Let $x_\ell$ and $x_{ij}$ for all $ij \in \binom{[\ell-2]}{2}$ be arbitrary distinct vertices in $B$ and let $X$ be the set consisting of these vertices. Using these we can find a subdivision $T(X)$ of $K_\ell^-$ in $H$ with vertex set $A \cup X$, branch vertices $x_1,\ldots,x_\ell$ and paths $P(i,j)$ for all $ij \in E(K_\ell^-)$, as follows. \begin{itemize} \item For all $i \in [\ell-1]$, the vertex $x_i \in A$ corresponds to $i \in V(K_\ell^-)$, and the vertex $x_\ell \in B$ corresponds to $\ell \in V(K_\ell^-)$. \item For all $ij \in \binom{[\ell-2]}{2}$, each $P(i,j)$ has precisely one internal vertex $x_{ij}$, which lies in $B$. For all $i \in [\ell-2]$ and $j \in \lbrace \ell-1,\ell \rbrace$, $P(i,j)$ is the edge $x_ix_j$. \end{itemize} Note that $T(X)$ exists because $H[A]$ is complete and $H[A \setminus \lbrace x_{\ell-1} \rbrace,B]$ is complete bipartite. Different choices of $X$ give rise to distinguishable $T(X)$ since $V(T(X)) = A \cup X$. Each $X$ has order $\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1$, so \begin{eqnarray*} s(K_\ell^-,G) &\geq& s(K_\ell^-,H) \geq \binom{|B|}{\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1} \geq \left(\frac{2t^{1-\eps}}{(\ell-1)\left(\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1\right)}\right)^{\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1}\\ & \geq &t^{(1-2\eps)\left(\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1\right)}= t^{(1-2\eps)(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)}, \end{eqnarray*} completing the proof of (iii).
nodes.statement_short: In the structure $H$ from Claim 5, each choice of $\binom{\ell-2}{2}+1$ vertices of $B$ gives a distinguishable $T(X)$, yielding $t^{(1-2\eps)(e(K_\ell^-)-2\ell+5)}$.

nodes.name: Characterisation of the exponential family
nodes.statement: The next theorem generalises Theorem~\ref{main} by describing the set of all graphs $F$ on $\ell$ vertices for which one can find $c,c' > 0$ such that whenever $t$ is a sufficiently large integer compared to $\ell$, we have $s_t(F,k) \geq c^{t^{c'}}$. Note that $(F,\ell,t)$-locally dense is the same as $(F,t)$-locally dense. So this notion seems to be the most natural strengthening of $(F,t)$-locally dense. As expected, the family of those $F$ of order $\ell$ giving rise to exponentially many subdivisions when the host graph is $(F,k,t)$-locally dense gets strictly larger as $k$ decreases. In fact $F$ lies in this family if and only if $F \supseteq K_k$.
nodes.statement_short: Under $(F,k,t)$-local density the exponential family is exactly $\{F : F \supseteq K_k\}$, and it grows as $k$ decreases.

nodes.name: Theorem 6 (spectrum of local conditions)
nodes.statement: Let $\ell,k \in \mathbb{N}$ and $3 \leq k \leq \ell$. Then, whenever $t$ is sufficiently large, the following hold. \begin{itemize} \item[(i)] For all graphs $F$ containing a copy of $K_k$, we have that $s_t(F,k) \geq 2^{t^{c'(k)}}$, where $c'(k) \geq \frac{1}{2(k-2)}$. \item[(ii)] For all $K_k$-free graphs $F$, we have that $s_t(F,k) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$. \end{itemize}
nodes.statement_short: Under $(F,k,t)$-local density, $s_t(F,k)$ is exponential in a power of $t$ exactly when $F \supseteq K_k$, and polynomial when $F$ is $K_k$-free.
conclusions: For all graphs $F$ containing a copy of $K_k$, we have that $s_t(F,k) \geq 2^{t^{c'(k)}}$, where $c'(k) \geq \frac{1}{2(k-2)}$.
For all $K_k$-free graphs $F$, we have that $s_t(F,k) \leq 2^\ell(t+2)^{e(F)+2\ell}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6
nodes.statement: For (i), let $F$ be a graph on $\ell$ vertices containing a copy of $K_k$. Let $G$ be a $(F,k,t)$-locally dense graph. Then $G$ is certainly $(K_k,t)$-locally dense. The conclusion follows immediately from Theorem~\ref{main}(i). For (ii), note that $F$ is $K_k$-free if and only if every subgraph $F' \subseteq F$ with $|F'| \geq k$ is such that $F'$ contains a pair of non-adjacent vertices. Therefore the graph $G$ we constructed in the proof of Theorem~\ref{main}(ii) is in fact $(F,k,t)$-dense. (To see this, one can use the same argument, as there is always a non-adjacent pair in $F'$ which can we embed into $B$ in at least $t$ different ways.) The conclusion follows from Lemma~\ref{semibip}.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce (i) to Theorem 2(i) by noting $(F,k,t)$-local density implies $(K_k,t)$-local density, and (ii) to Lemma 4 via the same construction.

nodes.name: Part (i) reduction to Theorem 2(i)
nodes.statement: For (i), let $F$ be a graph on $\ell$ vertices containing a copy of $K_k$. Let $G$ be a $(F,k,t)$-locally dense graph. Then $G$ is certainly $(K_k,t)$-locally dense. The conclusion follows immediately from Theorem~\ref{main}(i).
nodes.statement_short: $(F,k,t)$-local density implies $(K_k,t)$-local density, so Theorem 2(i) applies.

nodes.name: Part (ii) reduction to Lemma 4
nodes.statement: For (ii), note that $F$ is $K_k$-free if and only if every subgraph $F' \subseteq F$ with $|F'| \geq k$ is such that $F'$ contains a pair of non-adjacent vertices. Therefore the graph $G$ we constructed in the proof of Theorem~\ref{main}(ii) is in fact $(F,k,t)$-dense. (To see this, one can use the same argument, as there is always a non-adjacent pair in $F'$ which can we embed into $B$ in at least $t$ different ways.) The conclusion follows from Lemma~\ref{semibip}.
nodes.statement_short: $K_k$-freeness gives a non-adjacent pair in every large $F'$, so the Theorem 2(ii) construction is $(F,k,t)$-dense and Lemma 4 applies.

nodes.name: Summary of the characterisation
nodes.statement: We have shown that among all graphs $G$ which are $(F,t)$-locally dense, for large $t$ the minimum number of distinguishable subdivisions of $F$ in $G$ is exponential in a power of $t$ if and only if $F$ is a complete graph. Whenever $F$ contains a non-adjacent pair of vertices, there is a simple construction of an $(F,t)$-locally dense graph $G$ of order $O(t)$ with a very small dominating set $A$ of order less than $|F|$. This property means that any subdivision of $F$ in $G$ cannot contain many vertices outside of $A$ which in turn implies $s(F,G)$ is polynomial in $t$.
nodes.statement_short: $s_t(F)$ is exponential in a power of $t$ iff $F$ is complete; otherwise a small dominating set forces polynomial behaviour.

nodes.name: Natural strengthenings are easy to handle
nodes.statement: When one strengthens the local condition on $G$ (in order to increase the family of graphs $F$ which give rise to exponentially many subdivisions) in the most natural way, it is easy to characterise this family using our earlier results.

nodes.name: Restating Tuza's question for a different local condition
nodes.statement: Therefore it would be of interest to restate the question of Tuza with an entirely different local condition. To be interesting, such a condition on the host graph $G$ cannot imply for all $F$ that $G$ has minimum degree at least some polynomial in $t$; otherwise Theorem~\ref{btks} and the argument in Theorem~\ref{main}(i) imply the desired conclusion.
nodes.statement_short: Find an interesting local condition on $G$ that does not already force minimum degree polynomial in $t$.

nodes.name: Vertex version of the local condition
nodes.statement: We remark that our proof of Theorem~\ref{main} also works when `edge' is replaced by `vertex' in our local condition: that is, we consider host graphs $G$ in which every vertex lies in at least $t$ copies of $F$.
nodes.statement_short: The proof of Theorem 2 also works with `vertex' in place of `edge' in the local condition.
